title: Hosted API control-plane sync stall — incident chronicle and follow-ups
summary: Between 2026-11-25 02:11 UTC and 2026-11-25 03:04 UTC the hosted API experienced a P1-scale degradation. Symptoms: elevated request latency across regions, intermittent 5xx for streaming endpoints, and partial streaming disconnects. Root cause was a control-plane membership sync stall that cascaded into routing instability and KV-cache lock contention on edge proxies. This doc collects timeline, investigation notes, mitigations, and action items for follow-up.
timeline:
02:09 UTC - Canary alert: SRE synthetic latency monitor shows 99th percentile increase in eu-central-1.
02:11 UTC - Pager triggered for p1 latency (alert threshold exceeded).
02:13 UTC - Oncall triage: streaming clients report reconnects; tail samples show backend requests queueing 50-200ms before service selection.
02:17 UTC - Engineering oncall pulls control-plane logs: repeated leader re-election messages and 'member absent' spikes.
02:22 UTC - Found config rollout (infra PR merged 02:05 UTC) that reduced control-plane heartbeat rate from 10s to 30s in a canary group.
02:25 UTC - Observed long GC pauses and lease refresh backpressure on router process; KV cache mutex hold times spiked.
02:30 UTC - Emergency rollback of the heartbeat change in canary group initiated.
02:36 UTC - Rollback complete for canary; control-plane membership stabilizes slowly but some proxies still show stalled state.
02:50 UTC - Manual restart of 12 router workers in eu-central-1 to clear mutex waits and rehydrate KV caches.
03:04 UTC - Metrics returned to baseline; paging status moved to monitoring.
03:20 UTC - Post-incident Slack sync: initial RCA hypothesis documented.
impact:
- Customer-facing: transient request latencies up to 800ms p99 for text generation; 1.2% streaming session resets in affected regions.
- Internal: increased error budget burn for hosted-api SLOs in eu-central-1 and us-west-2 during the window.
- Business: no major customer-reported data loss; some low-latency product features experienced degraded QoE.
investigation_notes:
- Control-plane leader churn correlated tightly with region latency traces.
- The config change that reduced heartbeat frequency caused longer detection/slowness for ephemeral members; in combination with a transient networking blip this allowed some routers to think certain backends were unhealthy.
- Routers protect themselves with per-backend mutexes for KV cache miss handling; when multiple requests hit cold keys the mutex contention held scheduling threads and caused request queuing for application-level selection.
- Streaming endpoints rely on timely route resolution; when route info lags, streaming handshakes sometimes fall back to older ephemeral connections which resulted in resets.
- GC traces on a subset of router hosts showed 200-600ms pauses that amplified the effect (went from small to noticeable due to the already-extended heartbeat window).
- Rate of reconnection attempts temporarily increased control-plane write load, which briefly delayed reconciliation loops.
root_cause: Primary: a mis-scoped config rollout that increased control-plane heartbeat interval from 10s to 30s for a canary group. This change reduced failure detection responsiveness. Secondary contributing: transient network packet loss in one AZ, and router-side KV-cache lock contention amplified by GC pauses on some hosts. The interaction of these three factors led to membership desyncs and request routing instability which manifested as latency spikes and streaming resets.
immediate_mitigation:
- Rolled back the heartbeat change in the canary group (02:30 UTC).
- Restarted affected router workers to clear mutex starvation and rehydrate KV cache (02:50 UTC).
- Increased alert sensitivity for membership churn to avoid slippage on slow heartbeats.
- Deployed a temporary runbook step for oncall: if membership churn > 3/min then consider rollback of recent membership-related config changes and perform targeted worker restarts.
long_term_actions: Add automated dry-run gating for control-plane heartbeat changes (simulate membership churn before allowing rollout)
Instrument per-router mutex hold-time SLI and set alerting for >50ms median hold-time over 5m
Add a defensive backoff in streaming handshake when route info is stale instead of immediate reset
Harden canary rollout workflow: require ember-sim tests + network-conditioning on canary before region-wide promotion
Investigate heap/GC tuning on router images; reduce pause variance and add jemalloc profiling to mitigate long-tail GC
Improve runbook: explicit steps for control-plane config rollback and safe router restart sequence to preserve in-flight streaming sessions
Postmortem writeup to product/ops and a short customer communication template for minor availability blips
runbook_changes:
- New entry: 'Control-plane heartbeat regression' with clear rollback commands and dashboard links.
- Added a preflight checklist to canary config change PRs: include simulated member loss, synthetic load with cold KV cache, and heartbeat sensitivity test.
- Clarified safe restart order for router workers to minimize streaming churn: drain connections, restart subset, verify KV cache warm-up, then proceed.
oncall_notes:
- If you see membership churn alert: check recent infra PR merges (look for heartbeat/lease/consensus changes).
- Prefer targeted actor restarts over full autoscaling cycles until membership stabilizes.
- If rolling back a control-plane change, watch reconciliation rate and route-age metrics; do not restart more than 25% of routers at once.
- Use the emergency channel #sre-incident-4521 and add 'incident-tag:control-plane' to the JIRA ticket for tracking.
- Estimated toil: ~1.5 engineer-hours for mitigation and ~8 engineer-hours for follow-up actions.
notes: This incident surfaced a brittle coupling between control-plane membership timing and router-side locking behavior. The long-term work aims to decouple route freshness from blocking cache operations and to tighten the guardrails around membership-sensitive config rollouts. Please review long_term_actions and add owners in next sync.
